datasets.title: Local power cuts from night lights (NASA Black Marble)
datasets.description: NASA Black Marble VNP46A2 daily night lights (2023-2024, BRDF and moonlight corrected), high-quality cloud-free nights only. A night counts as dark for a lit block (median 5.0+ nW/cm²/sr) when its radiance relative to its own median falls below 0.5 of that night's citywide median ratio, so haze and thin cloud that dim the whole city cancel out. About 500 m pixels, so ~1 km blocks. Sensor artefacts and street lights switched off also count; a high share is a lead to check with the distribution company, not a measured outage.
datasets.source: pipeline/realestate/blackouts.py (NASA Black Marble VNP46A2 via Earth Engine)

datasets.title: Climate 2050 (CMIP6, downscaled)
datasets.description: Heat and extreme rain by 2041–2060 against today. A six-model NASA NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 ensemble (ACCESS-CM2, EC-Earth3, MIROC6, MPI-ESM1-2-HR, MRI-ESM2-0, NorESM2-MM) gives the change from 1995–2014: hot-season (Mar–Jun) daytime and monsoon (May–Sep) night-time warming, added to every ERA5-Land day of 2015–2024 to count days ≥ 40 °C and nights ≥ 28 °C; and the ratio of the mean annual wettest day, applied to CHIRPS 2005–2024. Climate models are ~25 km and reanalysis ~9 km, so this is a city- and district-scale outlook: street-level heat comes from Land surface temperature.
datasets.source: NASA NEX-GDDP-CMIP6, ECMWF ERA5-Land and UCSB CHIRPS via Earth Engine (pipeline/cells/ee_layers.py)
datasets.license: NEX-GDDP-CMIP6: CC BY 4.0 (most models); ERA5-Land: Copernicus licence; CHIRPS: public domain

datasets.title: Satellite embeddings (AlphaEarth)
datasets.description: Google Satellite Embedding V1 (AlphaEarth Foundations): a 64-number summary per 10 m pixel of a year of optical, radar, thermal, terrain and climate data. Change catches new building, cleared land, new water and greening alike: it says how much, not what.

datasets.title: Protected monuments and ASI limits
datasets.description: Wikidata items in India with a heritage designation and coordinates (230 in this city's box): Monuments of National Importance, State Protected Monuments and other listings. Under the AMASR Act (amended 2010) no new construction is allowed within 100 m of a national monument's protected limits, and from 100 to 300 m it needs National Monuments Authority permission with height limits. Zones here are drawn from Wikidata's single point per monument, not the notified boundary, so they understate the limits around large sites; confirm with the ASI circle or NMA before buying or building.
datasets.source: pipeline/realestate/heritage.py (Wikidata SPARQL, P1435 heritage designation)

datasets.title: Humid heat 2050 (wet-bulb, CMIP6)
datasets.description: Afternoon wet-bulb temperature (Stull 2011, daily maximum temperature with the mean dew point) on every ERA5-Land day of 2015–2024, and the same days shifted by the six-model NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 change to 2041–2060 in March–September maximum temperature and relative humidity (ACCESS-CM2, EC-Earth3, MIROC6, MPI-ESM1-2-HR, MRI-ESM2-0, NorESM2-MM). Days at a wet-bulb of 28 °C or more are humid-heat days; 31 °C or more is where lab studies find healthy young people can no longer shed heat. A ~9–25 km city-scale outlook; reanalysis runs 1–2 °C cool in cities.
datasets.source: NASA NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 and ECMWF ERA5-Land via Earth Engine (pipeline/cells/ee_layers.py)
datasets.license: NEX-GDDP-CMIP6: CC BY 4.0 (most models); ERA5-Land: Copernicus licence

fields.label: Change in hot-season relative humidity by 2050 (SSP2-4.5)

datasets.title: Heat & humid heat (ERA5-Land)
datasets.description: Air-temperature heat stress for 2025 from ERA5-Land daily aggregates (~9 km reanalysis): days with a maximum ≥ 40 °C (the IMD plains heatwave threshold), nights with a minimum ≥ 28 °C, and afternoon wet-bulb (Stull 2011, daily max temperature with mean dew point) — humid-heat days are wet-bulb ≥ 28 °C. Reanalysis smooths the urban heat island and usually reads 1–2 °C below city stations; use Land surface temperature for street-scale contrast.
datasets.source: ECMWF ERA5-Land daily aggregated via Earth Engine

datasets.title: Lake health (Sentinel-2)

Only blocks with at least 2% water in either year are kept. One season's median swings with the monsoon before it, so read small changes as noise.

datasets.title: Roof albedo (Sentinel-2)

Cool-roof paint or lime wash reaches 0.6–0.8.

datasets.title: Subsoil for foundations (OpenLandMap)
datasets.description: Predicted clay content at 60 cm and 1 m and bulk density at 60 cm from OpenLandMap's 250 m soil maps. Under built-up land these are model predictions, not borehole results: get a soil test before building.

datasets.title: Traffic load (time-of-day model)
datasets.description: Modelled traffic on the arterial roads through the day: residents (GHSL) make 0.9 motorised trips a day toward jobs and activity floor space (GHSL non-residential built-up, OSM amenities), distributed by a gravity model and routed on the OSM arterial network with BPR congestion feedback. Three patterns are assigned: the 09:00 commute, the 18:00 trip home (the morning matrix reversed) and shorter midday errands; peak fields show the worse of the two peaks; 0.37 PCU per trip for an Indian mode mix, IRC 106 capacities. A strategic model, not traffic counts: no signals, lane counts, one-way rules or local streets.
datasets.source: pipeline/traffic/demand_model.py over OSM arterials (data/traffic) + GHSL + OSM amenities

datasets.title: Tree canopy through the seasons (Sentinel-2)
datasets.description: Sentinel-2 NDVI medians for 2025 (Mar-May and Aug-Oct), read only over tree canopy (Meta/WRI canopy ≥ 5 m at each 20 m sample). A proxy, not a species count.

datasets.title: Water risk now and 2050 (WRI Aqueduct)
datasets.description: WRI Aqueduct 4.0 per sub-basin (HydroBASINS level 6, split by state): water stress and depletion (PCR-GLOBWB 2, 1979–2019), groundwater table decline (1990–2014 trend), drought risk and access to drinking water and sanitation; and 2050 stress and depletion under business-as-usual (SSP3 RCP7.0), optimistic (SSP1 RCP2.6) and pessimistic (SSP5 RCP8.5) futures. The future runs use a different model set from the baseline, so compare 2030 with 2050, not baseline with 2050. Basin values cover the whole catchment, so every block in a basin gets the same number: a city-level outlook, not a block one.
datasets.source: WRI/Aqueduct_Water_Risk/V4 via Earth Engine (pipeline/cells/ee_layers.py)

datasets.title: Rain waterlogging
datasets.description: Where heavy rain pools, independent of rivers. Combines Sentinel-1 radar passes that saw standing water on normally dry land in the wet seasons 2021–2025 (VV under −16 dB and 3 dB darker than the Feb–Apr median after a 30 m median filter, outside JRC water), hollows below the surrounding 300 m (Copernicus DEM), the topographic wetness index and height above drainage (MERIT Hydro) and sealed surface (GHSL). The index weights near-drainage 25%, radar-observed water 25%, wetness 20%, hollows 15%, sealing 15%. Radar misses water between tall buildings (double bounce), so dense cores lean on terrain; drains and pumping are not modelled.
datasets.source: Copernicus Sentinel-1 GRD + Copernicus DEM GLO-30 + MERIT Hydro + JRC GSW + GHSL GHS-BUILT-S via Earth Engine
datasets.license: Copernicus open licence; MERIT Hydro CC BY-NC 4.0; GHSL/GSW CC BY 4.0

fields.label: Seen waterlogged by radar, wet seasons 2021–2025
